gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-kannada: Nippo's small letters stand almost as tall as its capitals, cut like bent wire with no swell anywhere. Anek Kannada, a plain sans, brings a high, squared-off lowercase and open terminals, and that tension is what makes the pairing click.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-latin: Nippo draws a single wire-like line at one width, with lowercase nearly capital height, and Anek Latin sets tall, open letters beneath it. One handles display with technical bite; the other handles sentences with sans-serif ease.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-malayalam: Sharp, wiry, and a bit mechanical: Nippo forms each glyph from a ribbon of constant width. Anek Malayalam does the quieter job, keeping caps and lowercase close in height while its curve tips stay unclosed.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-odia: Nippo glows like neon glass, its tube-like strokes holding small letters up near capital height. Anek Odia, a plain sans, leaves its rounds unlatched and keeps capitals only just above lowercase, so the pair feels tidy and modern.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-tamil: Anek Tamil reads big and round, its lowercase bowls full and its c and s shapes looking half unwrapped. Nippo's flat, wire-cut headings give that softness a crisp, technical edge.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anek-telugu: Anek Telugu reads with a rhythm of wide, tall bowls, its rounds left open like unlatched hooks. And Nippo, drawn like fine wire, gives that sans a thin, technical headline to lean against.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-anuphan: Clean is the first impression of Nippo, whose flat wire-cut strokes never swell or thin. Anuphan follows with big round lowercase bowls and open curves, giving the pair a crisp top and a generous sans underneath.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-arimo: Arimo is a sans-serif with a tall mean line and generous gaps where its rounded letters end. Nippo's wire-drawn headings never swell or thin, but over a long passage Arimo reads steady and unhurried.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-armata: Nippo's lowercase rises almost to capital height, drawn like wire with no thick-thin swing at all. But Armata gives a longer stretch of text a sans that breathes, with wide gaps between characters and large lowercase bodies.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-athiti: Technical to the core, Nippo cuts its headings like wire, with small letters standing almost capital-sized. But Athiti, a plain sans, does the friendlier work, keeping each s open and its mean line high for easy sentences.
